Sum of Squares of Medians

In any triangle, 3 × (sum of squares of sides) = 4 × (sum of squares of medians). i.e., 3(AB² + BC² + CA²) = 4(AD² + BE² + CF²).

Centroid Property

The centroid (G) of a triangle divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex. AG : GD = 2 : 1.

Median in Right-Angled Triangle

The length of the median to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse.</p

questions.question: When the price of an item was reduced by 25% then its sale was increased by x%. If there is an increase of 20% in the receipt of the revenue, then the value of x will be∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Revenue = Price × Sale

Price Ratio = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3

Revenue Ratio = 100 : 120 = 5 : 6

Sale Ratio = (Revenue Ratio ÷ Price Ratio) = (5/4) : (6/3) = 1.25 : 2

Percentage increase in sale (x) = [(2 − 1.25) ÷ 1.25] × 100 = (0.75 ÷ 1.25) × 100 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Price reduction = 25%, Revenue increase = 20%, Sale increase = x%.

Formula: Revenue = Price × Sale

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36ec4c79af229f74a01529e6efb20b1970b9d19ffb43e3d1793adc2aa6097934.png] 

Let initial Price = 100 and initial Sale = 100.

⇒ Initial Revenue = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 − 25% of 100 = 75

⇒ New Revenue = 10000 + 20% of 10000 = 12000

⇒ New Sale = New Revenue ÷ New Price

⇒ New Sale = 12000 ÷ 75 = 160

⇒ Increase in Sale = New Sale − Initial Sale = 160 − 100 = 60

⇒ Percentage increase (x) = (60 ÷ 100) × 100 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Percentage Change Formula

If two variables change by a% and b%, the net effect on their product is (a + b + ab/100)%. Here, −25 + x + (−25x/100) = 20.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then y%, the final value is Initial × (1 + x/100) × (1 + y/100).

Fractional Conversions

25% = 1/4 (Reduction factor = 3/4) and 20% = 1/5 (Increase factor = 6/5). Multiplying factor for sale = (6/5) ÷ (3/4) = 8/5 = 1.6.</p

questions.question: frac{{{{( {1 + cos theta } )}²} + {{sin }²}theta }}{{( {cose{c²}theta - 1} ){{sin }²}theta }} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 60° in the expression.

Numerator = (1 + cos 60°)² + sin² 60° = (1 + 0.5)² + (3/4) = 2.25 + 0.75 = 3.

Denominator = (cosec² 60° − 1)sin² 60° = (4/3 − 1) × (3/4) = 1/3 × 3/4 = 0.25.

Expression value = 3 ÷ 0.25 = 12.

Checking Option (4): 2 sec 60°(1 + sec 60°) = 2 × 2(1 + 2) = 4 × 3 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 secθ(1 + secθ).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: [(1 + cosθ)² + sin²θ] ÷ [(cosec²θ − 1)sin²θ]

Using Trigonometric Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and cosec²θ − 1 = cot²θ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77080a990fceac8a208f3a1139505b002df9362c62214dd2fb31a48b602f4c6b.png] 

Step-by-step simplification:

⇒ Numerator = 1 + 2cosθ + cos²θ + sin²θ

⇒ Numerator = 1 + 2cosθ + 1 = 2 + 2cosθ = 2(1 + cosθ)

⇒ Denominator = (cot²θ) × sin²θ = (cos²θ / sin²θ) × sin²θ = cos²θ

⇒ Final Expression = 2(1 + cosθ) ÷ cos²θ

⇒ Expression = 2/cos²θ + 2cosθ/cos²θ = 2sec²θ + 2secθ

⇒ Expression = 2secθ(secθ + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 2 secθ(1 + secθ).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

Standard Pythagorean identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relationships

Key reciprocals used: secθ = 1/cosθ and cosecθ = 1/sinθ. These are helpful in converting all terms to sine and cosine.

Substitution Method

For multiple-choice identity questions, substituting a standard angle (like 30°, 45°, or 60°) is the fastest way to verify options.</p

questions.question: If A is 28% more than B and C is 25% less than the sum of A and B, then by what percent will C be more than A (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let B = 100 units, then A = 128 units.

Sum of A and B = 100 + 128 = 228 units.

C = 75% of 228 = 171 units (since C is 25% less than the sum).

Difference (C − A) = 171 − 128 = 43 units.

Required % = (43 ÷ 128) × 100 ≈ 33.6%.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: A = B + 28% of B; C = (A + B) − 25% of (A + B).

Formula: Percentage Increase = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d63f90b2925be34904273ed6e14828299cc4257b5c370712a237da21132c603.png] 

⇒ Let B = 100

⇒ A = 100 × (128 ÷ 100) = 128

⇒ Sum (A + B) = 128 + 100 = 228

⇒ C = 228 × (75 ÷ 100) = 171

⇒ Difference between C and A = 171 − 128 = 43

⇒ Required Percentage = (43 ÷ 128) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 33.59375% ≈ 33.6%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison Base

Always identify the 'than' part in the question to determine the denominator (base). In 'C is more than A', A is the base.

Fractional Equivalents

Using fractions can speed up calculations: 25% less means 3/4 of the value, and 20% more means 6/5 of the value.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes a% and b%, the net change is given by [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.</p

questions.question: frac{{( {2sin A} )( {1 + sin A} )}}{{1 + sin A + cos A}} is equal to∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Pick a specific value for angle A to test the options. Let A = 90°.

Then sin 90° = 1 and cos 90° = 0.

Expression = [2(1)(1 + 1)] ÷ (1 + 1 + 0) = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

Check options: (1) 1+0=1; (2) 1+1−0=2; (3) 1−0=1; (4) 1+0−1=0.

Only Option (2) gives the result 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sin A − cos A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Expression = [2 sin A (1 + sin A)] ÷ [1 + sin A + cos A]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7de93c83e8247749b029b3d007be532c41c0246cfda29f6096b817d3b13276ef.png] 

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin A − cos A).

⇒ Denominator = [(1 + sin A) + cos A] × [(1 + sin A) − cos A]

⇒ Denominator = (1 + sin A)² − cos²A

⇒ Denominator = 1 + sin²A + 2 sin A − (1 − sin²A)

⇒ Denominator = 1 + sin²A + 2 sin A − 1 + sin²A

⇒ Denominator = 2 sin²A + 2 sin A = 2 sin A (1 + sin A)

⇒ Expression = [2 sin A (1 + sin A) × (1 + sin A − cos A)] ÷ [2 sin A (1 + sin A)]

⇒ Expression = 1 + sin A − cos A

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sin A − cos A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identity: sin²A + cos²A = 1, which implies cos²A = 1 − sin²A and sin²A = 1 − cos²A.

Conjugate Multiplication

To simplify fractions with (a+b+c) in the denominator, group terms as ((a+b)+c) and multiply by ((a+b)−c) to use the difference of squares: (x+y)(x−y) = x² − y².

Value Substitution Method

Standard angles like 0°, 45°, and 90° are useful for checking trigonometric identities quickly, provided the expression is defined for those values.</p

questions.question: From the top of a tower, the angles of depression two objects on the ground on the same side of it, observed to be 60° and 30° respectively and the distance between the objects is 400√3 m. The height (in m) of the tower is∶
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In height and distance, for two angles θ₁ and θ₂ on the same side of a tower of height h:

Distance between objects (d) = h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)

Given: d = 400√3 m, θ₁ = 30°, θ₂ = 60°

400√3 = h(cot 30° − cot 60°) = h(√3 − 1/√3) = h(2/√3)

h = (400√3 × √3) ÷ 2 = (400 × 3) ÷ 2 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle of depression 1 = 60°

Angle of depression 2 = 30°

Distance between objects = 400√3 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c08cddb3c9398491981dd5b9dc43fcc46f4fcaf26299dd416bb8f55e712ccf19.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the height of the tower CD be h and the distance BC be x.

In right-angled triangle ▵BCD:

⇒ tan 60° = h ÷ x

⇒ √3 = h ÷ x

⇒ x = h ÷ √3 —— (1)

In right-angled triangle ▵ACD:

⇒ tan 30° = h ÷ (x + 400√3)

⇒ 1/√3 = h ÷ (h/√3 + 400√3) [From (1)]

⇒ h/√3 + 400√3 = h√3

⇒ 400√3 = h√3 − h/√3

⇒ 400√3 = (3h − h) ÷ √3

⇒ 400√3 = 2h ÷ √3

⇒ 2h = 400√3 × √3

⇒ 2h = 400 × 3

⇒ h = 1200 ÷ 2

⇒ h = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression and Elevation

The angle of depression from the observer's eye to an object below is equal to the angle of elevation from the object to the observer's eye (alternate interior angles).

Case: Objects on Opposite Sides

If two objects are on opposite sides of a tower of height h, the distance between them is d = h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂).

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

For height and distance, remember: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, cot 30° = √3, and cot 60° = 1/√3.</p
